full_text_en:
Xizhuang Village Committee v. Changdao County Shipping Company
— Dispute over Damages for Tortious Sand Mining on Shoal (Appeal)

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Changdao County Shipping Company, Shandong Province.
Legal Representative: Hu Yutian, Manager.
Agents ad litem: Su Yonghong, Tong Dezhong, Lawyers of Changdao County No. 1 Law Office, Shandong Province.

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance): Xizhuang Village Committee, Dengzhou Town, Penglai City, Shandong Province.
Legal Representative: Li Bengui, Director.
Agents ad litem: Zhang Qing, Lawyer of Bo'ai Law Office, Qingdao; Cui Demin, Manager of Penglai Mineral Development Company.

The Appellant, Changdao County Shipping Company, Shandong Province (hereinafter referred to as the Shipping Company), appealed to the Shandong High People's Court against the judgment of the Qingdao Maritime Court at first instance in the dispute with the Appellee, Xizhuang Village Committee, Dengzhou Town, Penglai City, Shandong Province (hereinafter referred to as Xizhuang Village), over damages for tortious sand mining on a shoal.

Facts Found by the Court at First Instance:
In the late 1980s, the phenomenon of seawater erosion on the coast west of Xizhuang Village intensified. In many areas, the sandy beaches had disappeared and land was washed away. From 1985 to 1993, the coastal land area of Xizhuang Village decreased by 165.29 mu (approximately 11.02 hectares), resulting in direct economic losses of RMB 3,436,500. The estimated cost of bank protection works to prevent further losses was over RMB 5,612,000.

In April 1990, the Yantai Municipal Government engaged the Yantai Marine Management District of the State Oceanic Administration (hereinafter referred to as the Yantai District) to investigate and demonstrate the situation of coastal erosion in Xizhuang Village. The Yantai District produced a report titled "Investigation and Study on Coastal Erosion West of Xizhuang, Penglai County" in early September 1990. In mid-September 1990, the Yantai Municipal Government invited 11 marine experts to review the report. The review opinion concluded that the coastal erosion west of Xizhuang Village was caused by years of natural evolution, storm waves, and man-made sand mining on the shore. The Dengzhou Shoal had a certain effect in mitigating the impact of waves, currents, and storm waves on this coastline. The shoal west of Chaodaizhou had little effect due to its distance from the shore.

On November 15, 1990, the Penglai Municipal Government commissioned the First Institute of Oceanography of the State Oceanic Administration (hereinafter referred to as the First Oceanography Institute) to study "the causes of coastal erosion, the possible extent of coastal erosion development, and the main countermeasures and methods to solve the erosion problem." The First Oceanography Institute submitted a report titled "Study on the Causes and Control Measures of Coastal Erosion from Xizhuang to Luanjiakou, Penglai" in December 1992. The report concluded that the causes of coastal erosion from Xizhuang Village to Luanjiakou were natural erosion, sand mining on the shore, and damage to the Dengzhou Shoal, with sand mining on the Dengzhou Shoal being the main reason for the acceleration of coastal erosion in that section. The report was awarded a "Certificate of Scientific and Technological Achievement Appraisal" by the Shandong Provincial Science and Technology Commission.

The Dengzhou Shoal is located in the sea area approximately 1.5 km from Xizhuang Village, forming an angle of about 45° with the coastline, running from southeast to northwest. The shoal consists of Siren Zhou, Erri Zhou, Chaodai Zhou, and Xinjing Zhou. Within the 5-meter isobath on the 1974 edition chart, the minimum water depth of the shoal was 1.1 meters, the average water depth was 3.2 meters, and the area was 3.96 square kilometers. According to field measurements by the First Oceanography Institute in November and December 1990, the area within the 5-meter isobath of the Dengzhou Shoal had shrunk from 3.96 square kilometers in 1974 to 0.5 square kilometers, and its average water depth had also decreased by 1.1 meters.

The Defendant, the Shipping Company, began sand mining on the Dengzhou Shoal in July 1986 and obtained a "Temporary Mining Permit" valid for two years on September 16, 1989. On January 10, 1991, the Yantai Municipal Bureau of Mineral Resources and Administration issued a notice prohibiting any unit or individual from sand mining in the Dengzhou Shoal area from February 1, 1991, but the Shipping Company did not stop sand mining until May 21, 1991. From 1987 to 1991, the total amount of sand mined by the Shipping Company on the Dengzhou Shoal was 969,849 tons. Other units that also mined sand on the Dengzhou Shoal included Changdao County Quezui Shipping Company and Yantai Port Construction Company, but their sand mining volumes were less than those of the Defendant. In addition, the Plaintiff, Xizhuang Village, had organized villagers to dig and sell sand from the eroded coastal beach from the late 1970s to 1986. Other coastal villagers had similar situations, and the amount of sand mined was difficult to quantify. The Plaintiff admitted to an annual sand mining volume of approximately 3,000 to 5,000 tons.

Given that the case involved complex professional issues and that there were two investigation reports with different conclusions, the court commissioned the Institute of Oceanology of the Chinese Academy of Sciences (hereinafter referred to as the Institute of Oceanology, CAS) on October 18, 1994, to verify the scientific validity of the two reports. The institute assigned five researchers and associate researchers specializing in marine environment, marine waves, ocean currents, coastal engineering geology, and marine geology to conduct the verification. On May 15, 1995, they issued the "Verification Report of the Institute of Oceanology, Chinese Academy of Sciences on the Causes of Accelerated Coastal Erosion in the Xizhuang Area, Penglai." The report stated that the First Oceanography Institute's report "had more field measurement data, with comprehensive discussion and analysis," and that "the chapters on the analysis of coastal erosion causes were relatively objective." The report also concluded that "the main cause of accelerated coastal erosion in Xizhuang was the regression of the Dengzhou Shoal, and the direct cause of the shoal's regression was large-scale man-made sand mining on the Dengzhou Shoal."

Opinion of the Court at First Instance:
The court held that the Institute of Oceanology, CAS is an authoritative institution in the field of marine scientific research in China, and the personnel it assigned for verification were all competent and reasonably constituted. During the verification process, the personnel carefully studied and reviewed the investigation reports submitted by both parties and the supporting data, and sought the opinions of relevant experts. Therefore, their conclusion was prudent, serious, objective, comprehensive, scientific, and fair, and could serve as the basis for fact-finding, evidence adoption, and liability allocation in this case. The Defendant, the Shipping Company, engaged in long-term, large-scale sand mining on the Dengzhou Shoal, which was one of the causes of the accelerated coastal erosion damage suffered by the Plaintiff, Xizhuang Village. The Shipping Company's sand mining activities before obtaining the "Temporary Mining Permit" infringed upon the lawful rights and interests of Xizhuang Village and should bear tort liability in accordance with Paragraph 2 of Article 106 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China. Article 30, Paragraph 3 of the Mineral Resources Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "Where mining of mineral resources causes losses to the production or livelihood of others, the mining unit shall be liable for compensation and shall take necessary remedial measures." Although the Shipping Company had no subjective fault for its sand mining activities after obtaining the "Temporary Mining Permit," it should still bear civil liability in accordance with Paragraph 3 of Article 106 of the General Principles of the Civil Law, which provides: "Where there is no fault, but the law requires that civil liability be borne, such liability shall be borne." The damage suffered by Xizhuang Village was caused by multiple factors, including natural erosion, sand mining on the shore, and the regression of the Dengzhou Shoal. The Shipping Company could only bear liability for compensation corresponding to its own conduct. Xizhuang Village's claim that the Shipping Company should bear full liability was not established. Accordingly, the court at first instance rendered the following judgment:
1. The Defendant, the Shipping Company, shall compensate the Plaintiff, Xizhuang Village, RMB 945,000 for land losses caused by coastal erosion. Other losses shall be borne by Xizhuang Village itself.
2. The Defendant, the Shipping Company, shall compensate the Plaintiff, Xizhuang Village, RMB 1,559,800 as expenses for taking necessary protective measures to prevent further loss.
Court acceptance fee of RMB 64,010 and verification fee of RMB 15,000: Xizhuang Village shall bear RMB 57,282.25, and the Shipping Company shall bear RMB 21,727.76.

Appellant's Allegations:
The Appellant, the Shipping Company, appealed against the judgment at first instance, arguing: The verification report on which the first instance judgment was based had not been verified by facts and lacked objectivity; the report failed to consider many factors, such as the impact of port construction, marine aquaculture, the amount of sand mined on the Dengzhou Shoal, and the start time of sand mining, and thus lacked scientific validity; the report represented the opinions of individuals and could not represent the Institute of Oceanology, CAS, and thus lacked reliability. The Appellant applied for a new verification and requested the judgment be amended according to law.

Appellee's Defense:
The Appellee, Xizhuang Village, argued that the verification conclusion on which the first instance judgment was based was scientific and fair, and the judgment was lawful and correct. It requested that the appeal be dismissed and the judgment be affirmed.

Opinion of the Shandong High People's Court:
The facts found by the court at first instance were all supported by materials, certificates, investigation reports, and records of statements from the parties, which had been examined and cross-examined at trial and could be accepted. The Institute of Oceanology, CAS is an authoritative institution in marine research in China. The verification of the scientific validity of the two investigation reports from the Yantai District and the First Oceanography Institute, commissioned by the court at first instance, was procedurally lawful and could serve as the basis for fact-finding, evidence adoption, and liability allocation in this case. The Appellant's claim that the verification represented the opinions of individuals and could not represent the Institute of Oceanology, CAS was not established. The Appellant's application for a new verification on the grounds that the verification content was incomplete, had not been tested in practice, and that there were differences in academic opinion was rejected. The court at first instance found the facts clearly, applied the law correctly, and the judgment should be affirmed. Accordingly, the Shandong High People's Court, pursuant to Subparagraph (1) of Paragraph 1 of Article 153 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment:

Dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment.

Court acceptance fee for the second instance of RMB 64,010 shall be borne by the Appellant, Changdao County Shipping Company.
